chunks: From him, from Wahb, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who partners with another man in a commodity, and one indicates it to the other: he said, 'If there is profit, it is for him; and if there is a loss, it is upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on profit and loss distribution in Islamic partnership when one partner provides goods and the other provides labor?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of risk-sharing in *shirkah* (partnership), where the active partner bears the loss if the commodity depreciates, reflecting the Shia juristic view that profit is tied to risk-bearing. It highlights the distinction between capital contribution and managerial effort, a foundational concept in Islamic commercial jurisprudence (*fiqh al-mu'amalat*).
